Chapter 10: Legacy, Hope, and the Ongoing Work of Change
When you look back at a journey that started in the suburbs and led all the way to the spotlight of public life, it feels both unlikely—and somehow, meant to be. The road was anything but straight, packed with hurdles and unexpected turns. But through every twist, there was always this steady thread of purpose. That deep-down belief that just one person can make a real difference—and that the work of creating change is never truly finished.
Now, “legacy”—that’s a word people toss around a lot, isn’t it? But for her, legacy isn’t about statues or front-page headlines. It’s about something far more personal: the lives you’ve touched, the doors you’ve helped unlock, and the example you leave behind for those who follow. The work doesn’t stop with a single accomplishment. It carries on—through foundations, through advocacy, and in the quiet, everyday acts of service that usually fly under the radar.
There’s a real sense of pride in watching folks she once mentored step into leadership roles, and in seeing new faces rise up to keep fighting for justice and equality. That’s when you realize—the impact goes way beyond any single moment or job title.
Hope, she’s discovered, isn’t just a feeling you get on a good day. It’s actually a practice—a choice you make, over and over. It means pressing forward, believing that change is possible, even when it feels like the odds are stacked against you. Hope lives in the courage of everyday people—teachers, nurses, activists, parents—who keep showing up, working quietly to make things better for everyone around them.
Sure, the world still throws up plenty of challenges. But it’s also filled with possibility—if you’re willing to look for it.
Here’s the thing: this story doesn’t wrap up with one win or one loss. Change is a journey, not a destination. It’s about staying open—learning, growing, serving—no matter what. The lessons learned through a life in public service are simple, but they sure aren’t easy: keep showing up, speak the truth, put in the work, and never let go of the idea that tomorrow really can be better than today.
